stem: A child has an upper neck swelling and a fluctuant, bluish mass in the floor of the mouth; what is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Plunging ranula is the most likely diagnosis. It classically presents as a fluctuant, bluish floor-of-mouth mass that may extend into the upper neck by plunging through the mylohyoid.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because reactive lymphadenopathy usually causes a mobile, tender node after infection, not a bluish floor-of-mouth mass.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because a dermoid cyst is typically a midline congenital cystic swelling and does not usually present as a bluish lesion in the floor of the mouth with neck extension.
optionExplanations.C: Correct because a plunging ranula is a mucus extravasation pseudocyst from salivary tissue that presents as a fluctuant, bluish floor-of-mouth swelling and can extend into the neck.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because an epidermoid cyst is a congenital cystic lesion, but it does not classically cause a bluish floor-of-mouth mass with upper neck swelling.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because a lymph node abscess would present as an inflamed tender neck mass rather than a fluctuant bluish mass in the floor of the mouth.
